description: The whole of what the window is allowed to do: listen for the two events the Rust shell emits, and call the six commands `main.rs` registers - three ACP calls `heddle acp-agent` already serves, plus two reads through the very `heddle_connectors::FsRoot` the agent's own fs tools resolve every path through, plus one read-only report of the launch the child was spawned from. Deny-by-default is Tauri's own model here (Constitution VI) - this grant is `core:default` and `core:event:default` and nothing more, so the frontend still has no shell, no filesystem, no HTTP and no process permission of its own: it cannot spawn an agent, open a directory or reach a provider even if its code tried to. The Code view is not an exception to that. It never touches a file; it asks the Rust shell, which answers only inside the one directory the operator named with HEDDLE_UI_FS_ROOT and refuses every path that leaves it - the same refusal, from the same primitive, that the agent gets.
